priority_scale.Must: Essential; mandated by stakeholders, law or the core purpose. Without it the release fails.
priority_scale.Should: Important and expected, but a workaround exists or it can follow shortly.
priority_scale.Could: Desirable improvement (nice to have); included if time and budget allow.
priority_scale.Won't: Explicitly agreed to be left out of the current release (deferred).

scope_summary: The product is a centralized management reporting and analysis system for a large library consortium with many branches and shared library data. Its primary users are library staff, managers, directors, local and global administrators, and other authorized personnel; patrons interact only indirectly through the public catalog or library displays. It supports reporting and analysis for collections, inventory, capacity, circulation, holds, patrons, finances, data quality, transfers, and operational oversight. The product reads and analyzes data from enterprise library-automation modules and integrates with related systems, but does not replace patron-facing catalog functions or manage core acquisitions, cataloging, or circulation workflows.

glossary.definition: A branch, facility, or other organizational site at which library materials, staff, transactions, or financial activity are associated.
An organizational library entity that contains or administers one or more library locations.
The overall network of participating library systems and locations managed through the centralized product.
An authorized employee or worker who uses management, reporting, or operational functions.
A management user responsible for supervising a library location or organizational unit.
An administrator responsible for local configuration, permissions, and reporting for a library system or location.
An administrator responsible for system-wide configuration, permissions, software changes, and consortium-level reporting.
An executive user who plans and directs library services, priorities, and strategic activities.
A person whose library account, activity, demographic attributes, or financial obligations are analyzed by the system.
A record representing a physical or otherwise individually managed library item, including its location, status, condition, value, and circulation history.
A catalog record describing a title or work to which item records may be attached.
A catalog hierarchy record that groups item records under a bibliographic record in the library system.
Library material tracked for inventory or circulation without an individual catalog record.
A generated presentation of selected, aggregated, or historical library data according to defined criteria.
A reusable definition of report criteria, fields, formatting, permissions, and output behavior.
A pre-defined report supplied with the product and intended to run with limited modification.
A report generated when requested, using preset logic that may allow selection or display criteria to be changed.
A report designed by selecting available record fields, filters, operators, and display options.
A structured specification for selecting, filtering, joining, grouping, or aggregating records.
The ordered processing mechanism for submitted reports, including waiting, running, completed, and failed states.
A data store or reporting environment containing historical or otherwise separated data for reporting without disrupting operational processing.
A recorded event involving the lending, return, renewal, or use of library material.
A circulation transaction that lends an item to a patron or records an equivalent use.
A circulation transaction that extends the loan period of an item.
A patron request to reserve or obtain an item or title when it becomes available.
An item recorded as moving between a sending and destination library location and not yet received.
An operation that changes the assigned location of one or more items and may coordinate their physical movement.
The measured ability of a library location or system to accommodate items, shelf space, circulation workload, or processing volume.
The physical or estimated space occupied or required by a collection of items.
The quantity of library material calculated from acquisitions, items at their library location, and items in circulation.
The process of identifying and removing, discarding, or changing the status of items according to collection-management criteria.
The audit record of deleted records, including the record type, identity, actor, time, location, and related details.
A recorded monetary event involving patron charges, fines, waivers, payments, bills, or ecommerce activity.
Authorization in which permissions are assigned through security groups or roles rather than individually managed permissions.
Information that can identify or be linked to an individual patron.
A machine-readable bibliographic record format whose fields may be selected, displayed, or validated in reports.
The patron-facing catalog interface through which patrons search library holdings and may perform supported account activities.

requirements.name: Save And Share Queries
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to save and share queries for repeated use so that staff members can reuse commonly run queries and share them with colleagues. Saved queries support recurring operational workflows such as monthly runs and can be treated similarly to Report templates for distribution and reuse. This feature improves efficiency by avoiding repeated query construction.
requirements.priority_rationale: The requirement is described as 'crucial' and 'need', indicating essential functionality.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Staff Productivity And Workflow Analysis
requirements.description: The system shall support analysis of staff member productivity and workflow so Library managers and administrators can assess operational efficiency and staff activity patterns. Analysis shall use staff-related operational data to report on productivity and workflow metrics.
requirements.priority_rationale: No explicit mandatory wording; described as an analytical capability expected by stakeholders.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Local Administrator Configuration
requirements.description: The system shall allow Local System Administrators to configure local settings and run system reports so individuals who oversee Library processes at the Library location can adapt settings and produce reports for their Library location. Local System Administrators shall have the elevated permissions necessary to perform local configuration and reporting tasks.
requirements.priority_rationale: The evidence describes expected administrative capabilities without mandatory wording, so assign Should.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Manager Reporting For Planning
requirements.description: The system shall provide reports for Library Managers to support planning and evaluation so managers can use report outputs to make operational and programmatic decisions for their organizational units. Reports shall target the planning and evaluation needs of Library managers.
requirements.priority_rationale: No mandatory cue; requirement describes expected reporting support for managers.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Aggregated Reports For Directors
requirements.description: The system shall provide aggregated, high-level reports for library directors to support strategic planning and board presentations, delivering summarized metrics and trends appropriate for executive decision-making. These aggregated reports shall enable library directors to prepare materials such as board reports and strategic analyses across the consortium and constituent Library locations.
requirements.priority_rationale: The evidence describes an expected capability for directors but uses non-mandatory language, so assign Should.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Report Template Creation And Management
requirements.description: The system shall allow system administrators to create report templates that are available to staff members and can be run as-is or modified for individual needs so administrators can publish consistent starting points while letting staff tailor display where permitted. Template management shall support template availability and the ability to run templates without modification or with permitted edits.
requirements.priority_rationale: Cue: 'need/needs to' indicates an expected capability but not explicitly mandatory in constraint language.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Run Or Customize Report Templates
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to run report templates, including canned reports, as-is or to modify their permitted display options for individual needs so staff users can either execute predefined reports or adjust display settings where allowed. Modifications shall be limited to display options permitted by report permissions while preserving the underlying canned report definitions.
requirements.priority_rationale: The evidence states this as an expected capability without mandatory language, so assign Should.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Template Change Integrity
requirements.description: The system shall ensure that changes to report templates do not compromise the accuracy or consistency of their results and criteria so that standardized reports produce consistent outputs across users and time. Template editing and versioning shall preserve result accuracy and allow consistent replication of named reports.
requirements.priority_rationale: No explicit obligation language; maintains important quality attribute of consistency tied to stakeholder concern.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Fine-Grained Report Permissions
requirements.description: The system shall provide distinct, fine-grained permission levels that limit who can create, clone, or add canned reports so that the ability to manage report content is controlled by role and permission. Permission controls must distinguish among actions such as creating new reports, cloning existing reports, and adding canned reports, ensuring only authorized Staff members and administrators can perform those actions. This supports governance of report proliferation and quality control.
requirements.priority_rationale: Stakeholders stated 'We need' fine-grained permissions; requirement framed as necessary but without absolute mandatory phrasing.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Shared Folders For Report Access
requirements.description: The system shall allow system administrators to create shared folders that control which Staff members may run specific reports and which sets of data Staff members may run on-demand reports against, enabling administrators to manage report visibility and data scope per group. Shared folders function as an access and scoping mechanism to permit or restrict report execution and ad hoc query targets for defined staff groups. This supports controlled distribution of reports and data access across the organization.
requirements.priority_rationale: Sources state administrators 'should' be able to create shared folders; described as a needed administrative control without mandatory phrasing.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: User-Friendly Query Designer
requirements.description: The system shall provide a user-friendly interface for designing queries against bibliographic records, item records, patron records, circulation transactions, and financial transactions, allowing Staff members to select fields, select values from picklists, select regular expressions from a drop-down menu, and use Boolean operators. The query designer must expose the relevant record types and let staff build queries via field selection, picklists of possible values, regex selection, and Boolean composition to produce report datasets. This enables staff to create reports without direct SQL coding while supporting expressive query capabilities.
requirements.priority_rationale: Sources describe this as a desired interface capability ('should', 'We need') but not framed as an absolute mandate.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Control Access To Query Tool
requirements.description: The system shall allow administrators to control Staff member access to the query tool, including access to the database tables and fields used by the query tool, so that data exposure via ad hoc queries is limited by role and permission. Administrators must be able to restrict which tables and fields each staff account or role can query to enforce data governance and privacy policies. This supports security and compliance while enabling authorized analysis.
requirements.priority_rationale: Sources explicitly use 'should' to describe administrative control of query access.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Canned Board And Executive Reports
requirements.description: The system shall provide canned Board and Executive reports for library boards and other external consumers, including the basic statistics required by the Georgia Annual Report and Application for State Aid. These predefined reports shall present the standard statistics and formats used for board presentations and external reporting requirements.
requirements.priority_rationale: The evidence indicates these reports 'should' be provided and references statutory reporting needs, supporting a Should priority.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Display Query Selections With Results
requirements.description: The system shall present the query selections used to generate a report alongside the report results so staff members can see the criteria that produced those results and validate or reproduce the query in the future.
requirements.priority_rationale: Reviewer and evidence indicate this is a recommended behavior (uses wording 'should'); therefore rated Should.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Report Queue Position And Status
requirements.description: The system shall allow staff members to view their report's position in the Report queue, its status (for example waiting, running, completed, failed), submission time, and priority information so staff can understand queue progress and reduce unnecessary support contacts.
requirements.priority_rationale: The evidence uses non-mandatory language (needs to, should) and describes an important usability improvement, so rated Should.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Support Appendix A Reporting Definitions
requirements.description: The system shall support the reporting definitions described in the report examples in Appendix A, implementing the report definitions and metrics as specified in that appendix so report outputs match the provided examples. This ensures conformity between the system's reports and the documented reporting definitions.
requirements.priority_rationale: The evidence explicitly states 'must' for supporting the Appendix A reporting definitions, making it mandatory.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Support Appendix B Fine-Grained Reports
requirements.description: The system must support the fine-grained reporting requirements described in Appendix B so staff members can produce the detailed, granular reports specified in the attached specification.
requirements.priority_rationale: The statement and evidence include explicit 'must' indicating an essential requirement.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Three Reporting Interface Types
requirements.description: The system shall provide three reporting interfaces: (a) Canned reports consisting of pre-delivered report templates that users can select and run immediately or on recurring schedules, (b) on‑demand reports consisting of preset reports whose selection criteria and display options users can edit and run on demand, and (c) open-template reports that allow users to select attributes associated with circulation transactions, Patrons, items, financial transactions, and bibliographic records for filtering and display; these interfaces enable Staff member, library manager, Local administrator, and Global administrator to produce both standard and customized reports from the Reporting warehouse. The interfaces are intended to support centralized reporting and analysis without replacing core operational systems.
requirements.priority_rationale: The statement uses 'shall' to specify needed functionality but does not indicate a legal or essential mandate, so it is classified as Should.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Hover Tooltip For Report Titles
requirements.description: The system shall provide a quick-access interface that displays a descriptive pop-up when a Staff member hovers over the title of a canned report or report template, so that Staff members can see the report description without opening the report. This feature shall present the description in a small pop-up box directly tied to the report title in the report listing. The pop-up tooltip supports faster selection of appropriate reports and reduces navigation overhead when choosing predefined or template reports.
requirements.priority_rationale: Requirement evidence indicates the feature is currently missing and is needed (No), so it is important and expected but not phrased as mandatory.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Selectable Data Elements Retain Nulls
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to select the data elements to include in a report and shall retain null and blank fields in the resulting report data regardless of filtering or display choices so exported datasets preserve the full schema and missing-value information. This enables downstream processing, data quality analysis, and consistent imports into other systems. Users with reporting permissions shall be able to choose which elements appear while the system preserves nulls and blanks for included elements.
requirements.priority_rationale: No explicit obligation language; requirement is important and expected but a workaround exists.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Scheduling And Recurring Report Editing
requirements.description: The system shall allow a Staff member to schedule reports to run immediately (Run ASAP) or on recurring intervals of hourly, daily, weekly, monthly, or yearly, and shall allow Staff members to edit recurring reports by adding or removing report selections and by editing associated email addresses. The scheduling controls shall present the listed frequency options and provide an edit interface for existing recurring report definitions including the recipient email list and included report selections. This capability enables automated distribution and ongoing maintenance of recurring report configurations.
requirements.priority_rationale: Evidence shows current lack of capability and specifies needed functionality (No, needs to), making it important but not framed as legally mandated.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Report Output Formats
requirements.description: The system shall provide report output in Excel, HTML, and CSV formats so that Staff members can receive and consume report results in these widely used file types. The export functionality shall allow reports to be generated and downloaded or delivered in any of the three specified formats. Supporting these formats ensures compatibility with common analysis and presentation tools.
requirements.priority_rationale: Evidence explicitly states these formats are required (Excel, HTML, and CSV formats are required).
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Email Distribution And Address Book
requirements.description: The system shall allow a Staff member to enter email addresses for report distribution and shall deliver scheduled reports by email; the system shall also maintain an address book of regularly used addresses for distribution convenience. Staff members shall be able to specify recipient addresses when scheduling or editing report deliveries and select from saved addresses for repeat use. This capability facilitates automated distribution of report outputs to intended recipients.
requirements.priority_rationale: The evidence describes this as desirable ('would be great'), indicating an optional enhancement.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Configurable Comparative Columns
requirements.description: The system shall allow a Staff member to configure comparative report columns, enabling output columns such as prior-period circulation counts, prior-year circulation counts, and percentage differences between periods so that comparative trends are visible in a single result set. The configuration shall permit selecting which period columns to include (for example last month, previous month, previous year) and specifying computed percent-difference columns. This supports analysis of circulation trends across different timeframes.
requirements.priority_rationale: The requirement is an expected analytic capability without mandatory wording, so Should fits.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Report Queue Prioritization
requirements.description: The system shall allow a Staff member to prioritize certain report types so they move ahead of resource-consuming reports in the report queue, enabling higher-priority reports (for example a director's board report) to jump ahead of less critical ad-hoc queries. Priority controls shall affect the ordering in the report queue so prioritized report jobs are scheduled or executed before lower-priority, resource-intensive jobs. This ensures critical reports are delivered promptly despite competing workload.
requirements.priority_rationale: The evidence labels the ability to prioritize reports as crucial and provides a concrete critical example ('crucial').
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Upload Filter Values From Text File
requirements.description: The system shall allow a Staff member to upload a text file containing values such as barcodes or TCNs for use as report filters so that bulk identifier-based filtering is supported. The uploaded file contents shall be applied as filter values for report generation, enabling reports to be run against the supplied list of identifiers. This feature streamlines reports that target large lists of items or records identified externally.
requirements.priority_rationale: Evidence indicates the capability is missing (No) and desirable; it is important but not explicitly mandated.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Pivot Table Output
requirements.description: The system shall provide pivot table output for reports so Staff members can analyze aggregated data across dimensions within the reporting interface or export pivot-ready results. Pivot output shall allow aggregation and cross-tabulation of report data to support multidimensional analysis. Providing pivot-format results enables flexible summarization and exploration of report data.
requirements.priority_rationale: Evidence notes the feature is currently missing and desirable (No), making it an important capability but not labeled mandatory.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Proven Output Format Reliability
requirements.description: The system shall provide tested and proven output formats for reports so that Staff members can rely on the stability and correctness of exported report files. Output formats shall be validated to ensure they conform to expected structure and encoding for intended consumption by analysis tools and recipients. Ensuring tested output formats reduces risk of format-related failures when distributing or processing reports.
requirements.priority_rationale: The statement is a quality expectation without explicit mandatory language, so Should is appropriate.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Cancel Scheduled Or Running Reports
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to cancel a scheduled or currently running report and shall check for cancellation signals during report processing so that users can stop unwanted or obsolete report jobs. The system shall provide the ability to request cancellation for scheduled jobs and running jobs and the report processor shall poll or otherwise detect cancellation signals during execution. This capability reduces wasted processing and supports operational control by staff and administrators.
requirements.priority_rationale: No explicit obligation language; requirement is important and expected but a workaround exists.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Real-Time Reporting For Current Data
requirements.description: The system shall provide real-time reporting for reports that require current data so that Staff members can obtain up-to-the-moment information for time-sensitive queries such as items overdue today. Real-time reporting shall return results based on the current state of the source systems rather than only historical snapshots when the report requires immediacy. This capability supports operational decisions that depend on current system state.
requirements.priority_rationale: Evidence notes some reports need real-time data and current lack of capability (No), making it important but not framed as mandatory.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Historical Reporting Via Reporting Warehouse
requirements.description: The system shall provide historical reporting through a reporting warehouse that allows data to be retrieved for a specified date or date range and preserves the historical state of data even when the shelving location has changed so users can view past states of records. The reporting warehouse shall allow queries for data as of a given date range and preserve attributes such as shelving location as they existed on that date. This supports audits, historical analysis, and accurate past-state reporting for staff and administrators.
requirements.priority_rationale: No explicit obligation language; requirement is important and expected but a workaround exists.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Defined Report Selection Criteria
requirements.description: The system shall clearly define report selection criteria so that Staff members understand precisely which records and fields are included when running a report. Selection criteria descriptions shall be presented in the reporting UI and included in report metadata or headers to reduce ambiguity about the data returned. Clear definition of selection criteria improves reproducibility and interpretation of reports.
requirements.priority_rationale: The statement is an expected quality attribute without explicit mandatory wording.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Include Report Name And Date Range
requirements.description: The system shall include the report name and the selected date-range criteria in report results so that Staff members can quickly identify the report and the period covered when viewing outputs. The report metadata shall appear at the top or bottom of the results and explicitly show the date selection used to generate the report. This ensures clarity when reviewing or distributing report outputs.
requirements.priority_rationale: The requirement is a standard expectation for reporting outputs without explicit mandatory language.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: MARC Fields On Single Row
requirements.description: The system shall allow report templates to pull specified MARC fields and present those MARC fields on a single row of report data. This enables report consumers to see all requested bibliographic data for a bibliographic record in one row rather than spread across multiple rows. It supports easier analysis and export of bibliographic fields in reports.
requirements.priority_rationale: No explicit obligation language; the evidence states a clear reporting need without mandatory phrasing.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Transaction Filters By Time Workstation Staff
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to run reports that filter circulation transactions by specified date and time, by workstation, or by staff member. This enables auditors and managers to locate transactions that occurred at particular moments or by particular staff members for operational review and investigation. The feature is used for transaction-level reporting and oversight.
requirements.priority_rationale: No explicit obligation language; the evidence describes an important but not legally mandated reporting capability.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Clone Report Templates
requirements.description: The system shall allow users with the appropriate permission to clone an existing report template by creating a new report template based on that existing template. Cloning enables users to reuse report definitions and modify copies without altering the original template. This supports efficient creation of similar reports while preserving approved templates.
requirements.priority_rationale: The evidence uses the word 'need' indicating an expected capability but not a legal mandate.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Expose Database Fields For Reporting
requirements.description: The system shall make all database fields available for field selection in the report writer, subject to administrator-controlled access restrictions so that report authors can select needed fields while administrators restrict sensitive fields. This capability addresses current limitations where some database fields are not selectable and enables more complete filtering and reporting. Administrators retain control over which fields individual users may access in reports.
requirements.priority_rationale: No explicit obligation language; the evidence highlights a functional limitation that should be addressed.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Background Processing And Queuing
requirements.description: The system shall provide background processing and report queuing so long-running reports are processed without slowing down the circulation client or other production workflows. Queued background processing ensures complex or resource-intensive reports run asynchronously against reporting infrastructure and do not tie up production resources. This protects operational responsiveness while allowing users to run complex analytical queries.
requirements.priority_rationale: The evidence describes a major concern and states the system needs background processing/queuing to prevent report generation from slowing production.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Staff Report Content And Design
requirements.description: The system shall allow staff members to create report content and design services reflected in reports so that paid employees of PINES member libraries can author and shape reporting outputs. This capability enables staff members to be primary content creators for report templates and to configure how services are described and measured in reports.
requirements.priority_rationale: No explicit mandatory wording; described as the role of staff members and expected functionality.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Library Manager Supervision Support
requirements.description: The system shall allow Library Managers to supervise a single organizational unit and provide input to the design and implementation of library services by enabling access and reporting appropriate to a manager's supervisory scope. The system must therefore provide Library Managers with report access and tools scoped to their single organizational unit so they can review operations and contribute to service design and implementation. This supports managers' responsibilities for unit-level oversight and participation in service decisions.
requirements.priority_rationale: The requirement uses 'shall' but describes organizational responsibilities rather than an externally mandated need; assign Should.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Support Directors Planning And Direction
requirements.description: The system shall allow library directors to plan and direct library services and priorities by providing the reporting and analysis capabilities directors need to evaluate services, allocate resources, and set priorities. The system shall surface the reports, dashboards, and data elements that enable directors to make strategic and operational decisions. This supports executive oversight and consortium-level planning.
requirements.priority_rationale: No explicit obligation language; requirement is important and expected but a workaround exists.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Circulation Item Patron Financial Hold Reports
requirements.description: The system shall provide circulation, item, patron, financial, hold, and custom on-demand reports so that staff members and managers can generate predefined and on-demand analyses covering checkouts, check-ins, renewals, inventory, weeding, missing items, patron demographics, inactive accounts, fines, payments, and hold activity. These reporting capabilities shall support both canned reports and custom on-demand reporting needs across the consortium.
requirements.priority_rationale: No explicit mandatory wording; requirement enumerates expected report types and on-demand capability.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Fast Reporting At Peak Times
requirements.description: The system shall run reports quickly during busy hours and avoid long runtimes at peak times so that staff members can obtain timely information during operational demand. This performance requirement targets acceptable report runtimes and responsiveness across peak usage periods for the consortium.
requirements.priority_rationale: No explicit mandatory wording; expressed as a necessary performance concern but not labeled essential.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Discoverable Report Interface
requirements.description: The system shall provide an interface that makes it easy for staff members to find the reports they need so that users are not hindered by confusing navigation when accessing inventory, circulation, data quality, or other reports. The interface shall improve discoverability and access to both canned and on-demand reports for staff members and administrators across the consortium.
requirements.priority_rationale: No explicit mandatory wording; requirement expressed as a usability need to address confusion.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Excel Export Without Excess Duplicates
requirements.description: The system shall export data to Excel without creating excessive duplicate rows so that exported datasets are usable for analysis and reporting by staff and managers. The export function must avoid producing redundant rows that complicate downstream data analysis or require significant cleanup. This improves efficiency for staff who rely on Excel for ad hoc analysis and reporting.
requirements.priority_rationale: The statement uses 'shall' but provides no explicit mandatory external cue; assign Should as an expected capability.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Support Custom And Local Reports
requirements.description: The system shall support custom or local reports such as collection development reports, program attendance reports, and staff productivity reports so that library locations and administrators can produce reports tailored to local needs. The system shall allow creation and execution of local report definitions covering the common use cases identified, and permit authorized staff and managers to run those reports. This enables local reporting needs alongside consortium-level reporting.
requirements.priority_rationale: No explicit obligation language; requirement is important and expected but a workaround exists.
requirements.area: Reporting, Querying, and Report Administration

requirements.name: Material Volume Report
requirements.description: The system shall provide a Material Volume Report that, for a selected Library location at any point in time, queries item records whose library location equals the selected Library location and bases counts on new acquisitions, items on the shelf or checked in, and items out in circulation. The report shall group results by configurable categories including adult fiction and board books, show hold counts by category, and allow breakdowns such as total items in the Library location, number of holds, number of adult fiction items, and number of board books. This enables library managers to produce monthly board reports without manual aggregation across multiple screens.
requirements.priority_rationale: The statement is presented as a key requirement and 'should' in the evidence, so assign Should.
requirements.area: Collection, Inventory, Capacity, and Material Operations

requirements.name: Separate And Total Item Counts
requirements.description: The system shall provide separate counts for new acquisitions, items on the shelf, and items out in circulation, and shall also provide a total count that includes items out in circulation so staff members can see both component and aggregate volume. This allows managers to understand composition of material volume while counting checked-out items toward the overall total.
requirements.priority_rationale: The evidence frames this as a requested reporting detail without mandatory language, so it is prioritized as Should.
requirements.area: Collection, Inventory, Capacity, and Material Operations

requirements.name: Customizable Volume Categories
requirements.description: The system shall allow the categories used in the Material Volume Report to be customized by authorized staff members and shall include, as examples, adult fiction and board books; for each category the report shall show the number of holds. Customizable categories and per-category holds enable tailored breakdowns such as total items, number of holds, and category-specific counts for reporting needs.
requirements.priority_rationale: The requirement and evidence use 'should' and 'need' to request customizable categories and holds counts.
requirements.area: Collection, Inventory, Capacity, and Material Operations

requirements.name: Acquisition Date Tracking
requirements.description: The system shall track the acquisition date for items in the centralized data store so that reports and filters can reference when items were acquired. This tracked acquisition date supports time-based reporting such as additions over a period and point-in-time volume calculations.
requirements.priority_rationale: The evidence affirms the database already tracks acquisition date but does not mandate it as essential, so it is prioritized as Should.
requirements.area: Collection, Inventory, Capacity, and Material Operations

requirements.name: Historical Volume Reports
requirements.description: The system shall provide reports showing changes in material volume over time and shall include date filters so staff members and directors can perform historical comparisons and view volume at any point in time. These time-based reports enable analysis of trends and support management decisions based on historical volume data.
requirements.priority_rationale: The evidence describes this as 'definitely' useful and requests date-filtered historical comparisons, supporting a Should priority.
requirements.area: Collection, Inventory, Capacity, and Material Operations

requirements.name: Date-Range Acquisition Reports
requirements.description: The system shall provide date-range reports that show the volume added through acquisitions during specified periods, enabling staff members and directors to see how much material was added over intervals such as the last 30, 60, or 90 days. These reports rely on the tracked acquisition date to calculate additions for the requested periods.
requirements.priority_rationale: The evidence labels this as 'helpful' rather than mandatory, so it is prioritized as Should.
requirements.area: Collection, Inventory, Capacity, and Material Operations

requirements.name: Consortium Capacity Overview
requirements.description: The system shall provide an interface that aggregates and displays Collection capacity data for all Library locations in the Consortium using the centralized data store so that Library managers can see capacity across the entire Consortium, not only their own Library location. This view shall present an at-a-glance overview of which Library locations have available capacity and which do not to support operational decision making. The interface uses the centralized data store as the authoritative source for Collection capacity.

requirements.name: Drill-Down To Library Location
requirements.description: The system shall allow users to drill down from the consortium collection-capacity overview into an individual library location so that library managers can move from a system-level view to location-specific details. This drill-down supports investigation and local operational decisions based on consortium-level alerts or trends.
requirements.priority_rationale: The evidence uses 'should' to request drill-down capability, so it is prioritized as Should.
requirements.area: Collection, Inventory, Capacity, and Material Operations

requirements.name: Collection Capacity Color Coding

The color-coding shall be applied consistently in views that present collection capacity so library managers can quickly assess collection space conditions.

requirements.area: Collection, Inventory, Capacity, and Material Operations

requirements.name: Grouping Locations By Region

requirements.name: Reduce Password Sharing Risks
requirements.description: The system shall reduce security issues caused by password sharing and staff members leaving terminals logged in by implementing controls that discourage shared credentials and detect or prevent unattended sessions. These measures help mitigate the operational security problems that arise when staff rush and share passwords or forget to log out. The system's security controls should improve accountability and reduce unauthorized access.
requirements.priority_rationale: No explicit obligation language; the evidence describes a desired security improvement rather than a mandate.
requirements.area: Platform, Integration, Security, and Accessibility

requirements.name: Run Reports On Separate Warehouse
requirements.description: The system shall run reports against a separate reporting warehouse or replica rather than the production database so that reporting workloads do not interfere with live production operations. Using a reporting warehouse protects the circulation client and production services from heavy report queries and supports stable operational performance. Administrators shall manage the reporting warehouse to provide up-to-date read-only views for reporting purposes.
requirements.priority_rationale: The evidence states the need to separate reporting from production operations to avoid negative impact on production.
requirements.area: Platform, Integration, Security, and Accessibility

requirements.name: WorldCat Integration
requirements.description: The system shall integrate with WorldCat to support reporting needs that depend on WorldCat data such as last copy determinations and broader bibliographic context. Integration with WorldCat enables the consortium to augment local bibliographic data for reports and decision-making about last-copy status. The evidence identifies WorldCat integration as critical for certain reporting functions.
requirements.priority_rationale: The evidence labels WorldCat integration as CRITICAL.
requirements.area: Platform, Integration, Security, and Accessibility

requirements.name: PostgreSQL 8.3 Database Use
requirements.description: The system shall use PostgreSQL 8.3 for the database so that the reporting platform runs on the consortium's chosen database technology. This constraint dictates the database engine for storage of reporting and warehouse data and applies to deployments that support the consortium environment.
requirements.priority_rationale: Explicit statement that it runs PostgreSQL 8.3 for the database indicates an essential constraint.
requirements.area: Platform, Integration, Security, and Accessibility

requirements.name: Role-Based Access With Security Groups
requirements.description: The system shall implement Role-based access control using security groups and roles that allow access control for individuals, workgroups, and arbitrary staff groups, so permissions can be managed at multiple organizational scopes. Security groups and roles must enable assignment of rights and privileges to single staff members, to defined workgroups, and to ad hoc staff groups for flexible administration. This approach centralizes permission management and supports consistent enforcement of access policies.
requirements.priority_rationale: The evidence labels this requirement as 'essential' and uses imperative language, indicating it is mandatory.
requirements.area: Platform, Integration, Security, and Accessibility

requirements.name: Configurable Server OS And Browser Support
requirements.description: The system shall accommodate configured server operating-system choices and supported web browsers so that the consortium can deploy the reporting system on approved server platforms and provide staff members with compatible browser access. This constraint ensures the product can be installed into varying technical environments and meet local operational requirements.
requirements.priority_rationale: Described as technical constraints without mandatory wording; expected deployment requirement.
requirements.area: Platform, Integration, Security, and Accessibility

requirements.name: Avoid Denormalization For Reporting
requirements.description: The system shall not denormalize reporting data because stakeholders strongly recommend against denormalization for reporting to preserve data integrity and simplify maintenance. This constraint directs the data modeling approach for the reporting warehouse and analytics processes across the consortium.
requirements.priority_rationale: Phrase 'strongly recommend against' signals important guidance but not an explicit mandatory legal constraint.
requirements.area: Platform, Integration, Security, and Accessibility

requirements.name: Safe Training Environment
requirements.description: The training environment shall allow staff members to experiment without risking production data so that staff can learn and test reporting features safely. The environment must isolate training actions from the production reporting warehouse and production data to prevent accidental modification or exposure of live data. This ensures safe practice, onboarding, and experimentation without affecting operational systems.
requirements.priority_rationale: The statement expresses a clear need but lacks external mandate language; assign Should.
requirements.area: Platform, Integration, Security, and Accessibility

requirements.name: Handle EDI Ordering Data
requirements.description: The system shall handle EDI ordering data from vendors when that data is available so that the reporting system can incorporate vendor-provided ordering information into financial and acquisitions-related reports. The system shall accept EDI data when present while accommodating that EDI data may not be available from every Library location.
requirements.priority_rationale: No mandatory cue; statement notes need but also that data cannot be relied on universally.
requirements.area: Platform, Integration, Security, and Accessibility

requirements.name: Separate From Online Public Access Catalog
requirements.description: The management reporting system shall be separate from the Online Public Access Catalog so that the reporting and analysis product does not replace or interfere with patron-facing catalog functions. The system shall integrate with the Online Public Access Catalog for relevant data reads where required but operate as a distinct system for reporting and administrative use. This separation preserves the public catalog's role and limits the product to management reporting and analysis.
requirements.priority_rationale: No explicit obligation language; requirement is a constraint but a workaround may exist.
requirements.area: Platform, Integration, Security, and Accessibility

requirements.name: Read-Only For Acquisitions And Cataloging
requirements.description: The system shall not manage Acquisitions or Cataloging workflows and shall only read data from those modules so that core workflow systems remain the authoritative sources. This constraint requires the reporting system to ingest and analyze data from acquisitions and cataloging modules without performing operational management of those workflows.
requirements.priority_rationale: Explicit statement that the reporting system doesn't manage those workflows and only reads the data indicates a mandatory boundary.
requirements.area: Platform, Integration, Security, and Accessibility

requirements.name: Username/Password Fallback Authentication
requirements.description: The system shall allow staff members to log in using individual username and password credentials as a fallback to card-based login and shall not require card-based login, ensuring staff can access the system when card-based authentication is unavailable.
requirements.priority_rationale: The clause 'shall not require' and the authentication constraint create a mandatory security/access requirement, so rated Must.
requirements.area: General

requirements.name: Admin Control Over Template Filters And Fields
requirements.description: The system shall allow administrators to limit which filters and display fields of a Report template staff members may alter, permitting safe changes such as specifying call-number ranges and adding or removing display fields while preventing staff members from altering a Report template to display deleted items, so templates produce certified and dependable outputs.
requirements.priority_rationale: No explicit obligation words in the statement or evidence; it is an important governance feature so rated Should.
